title: sapid
text:
A reference dictionary for mapping taste descriptors to standardized terms. Includes original, translated, and simplified versions. Designed for generic/widely-used sensory attributes.



dictionary_generic




A data frame with 64 rows and 3 columns:


original


Original or raw descriptor (often in French)


translated


English translation


translated_simple


Simplified/harmonized English form





Used by data harmonization functions (e.g., harmonize_terms()) to standardize taste terminology across panelists and sessions.



doi:10.1016/j.crfs.2025.101043; Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/14616396

data(dictionary_generic)
head(dictionary_generic)

  original translated translated_simple

4    UMAMI      UMAMI             UMAMI
5    FRAIS      FRESH             FRESH
6     SALÉ      SALTY             SALTY

subset(dictionary_generic, original == "BOIS\u00c9")

  original translated translated_simple

title: sapid
text:
Load Bruker 1D proton NMR experiments, autophase, interpolate, exclude solvent/artifact regions before total-area normalization, merge overlapping detected peak positions within peak_width_ppm / 2, integrate peaks, cluster fractions using Hellinger (Euclidean on square-root areas) or Canberra distance with Ward’s minimum-variance hierarchical linkage (ward.D2), and export a dendrogram-aligned spectral figure and cluster group table.



cluster_nmr(
  nmr_dir = "./data/10043",
  output_figure = "./data/figures/figure_nmr.pdf",
  output_groups = "./data/groups.tsv",
  experiment_raw = "proton_00",
  experiment_ref = "proton_98",
  experiments_fractions = c("proton_17", "proton_18", "proton_19", "proton_20",
    "proton_21", "proton_22", "proton_23", "proton_24", "proton_25", "proton_26",
    "proton_27", "proton_28", "proton_29", "proton_30", "proton_31", "proton_32",
    "proton_33", "proton_34", "proton_35", "proton_36", "proton_37", "proton_38",
    "proton_39", "proton_40", "proton_41", "proton_42", "proton_43", "proton_44",
    "proton_45", "proton_46", "proton_47", "proton_48", "proton_50", "proton_51",
    "proton_52", "proton_53", "proton_54", "proton_55", "proton_56", 
     "proton_57",
    "proton_58", "proton_59", "proton_60", "proton_61", "proton_62", "proton_63",
    "proton_64", "proton_65", "proton_66", "proton_67", "proton_68", "proton_69",
    "proton_70", "proton_71"),
  experiments_to_fix = c("proton_69", "proton_70", "proton_71"),
  k = 7,
  peak_width_ppm = 0.01,
  ppm_min = 0,
  ppm_max = 14.85,
  area_min = 0,
  range_exclude_area = c(2.5, 2.6),
  range_without_peaks = c(0, 0.4),
  ylim = c(0, 5e+10),
  dist_method = c("euclidean", "canberra")
)







nmr_dir


Directory containing Bruker NMR experiment folders.




output_figure


Output path for the PDF figure.




output_groups


Output path for the TSV cluster groups table.




experiment_raw


Identifier of the raw extract experiment.




experiment_ref


Identifier of the reference experiment.




experiments_fractions


Character vector of fraction experiment IDs.




experiments_to_fix


Optional character vector of experiment IDs whose ppm axis should be aligned to experiment_ref.




k


Integer number of hierarchical clusters (default 7).




peak_width_ppm


Numeric integration peak width in ppm (default 0.01).




ppm_min


Minimum chemical shift in ppm (default 0).




ppm_max


Maximum chemical shift in ppm (default 14.85).




area_min


Minimum integrated peak area threshold (default 0).




range_exclude_area


Numeric length-2 ppm range excluded from normalization and clustering.




range_without_peaks


Numeric length-2 baseline noise ppm range.




ylim


Numeric length-2 y-axis limits for spectral traces.




dist_method


Distance metric on square-root-transformed peak areas: “euclidean” (default, Hellinger distance) or “canberra”.






Four chemometric refinements are applied:


Pre-normalization solvent exclusion: range_exclude_area (e.g., residual DMSO-d6 at 2.5–2.6 ppm) is excluded prior to AlpsNMR::nmr_normalize() so that solvent peak fluctuations do not distort total-area normalization across fractions.


Non-overlapping peak integration windows: Detected peak positions closer than peak_width_ppm / 2 are merged via single-linkage grouping to their mean chemical shift before integration, preventing double counting of multiplet splittings.


Zero-preserving Hellinger/Ward.D2 clustering: Sub-threshold peak areas (<= area_min) are set to 0 (not NA) prior to the Hellinger square-root transformation so that absent peaks contribute well-defined zero coordinates compatible with Euclidean/Hellinger and Ward.D2 minimum-variance geometry.


Dendrogram leaf-to-fraction alignment: After sorting the dendrogram (sort(dend)), leaf colors (lab.col) are matched back to frac_short via labels(dend) so each fraction receives its true cluster color.





Named list with elements figure and groups.




library("sapid")

cluster_nmr()

Four chemometric refinements are applied:


Pre-normalization solvent exclusion: range_exclude_area (e.g., residual DMSO-d6 at 2.5–2.6 ppm) is excluded prior to AlpsNMR::nmr_normalize() so that solvent peak fluctuations do not distort total-area normalization across fractions.

title: sapid
text:
Mathematical & Algorithmic Improvements

3-AFC psychometric MLE curve (fit_afc_psychometric(), plot_concentration()): Replaced the decorative 2-point sigmoid and hardcoded 0.12 mg/L threshold with a guessing-corrected binomial log-logistic MLE (\(\gamma = 1/3\), Gaussian (L2) log-slope penalty \(\lambda = 0.05\)), delta-method 95% confidence ribbons, and analytical \(\text{EC}_{50}\) threshold (\(0.525\text{ mg/L}\) at \(P = 2/3\)). Preserved individual juror ratings in Panel A violins instead of per-taste means.
Pratt’s zero-preserving signed-rank test (pratt_wilcox_pvalue(), plot_chasselas_modulation()): Replaced the binomial sign test with Pratt’s (1959) zero-preserving Wilcoxon signed-rank test (test_method = "pratt"), retaining zero differences during ranking with exact zero- and tie-variance corrections.
Greiner’s Kendall-to-Pearson transformation, local RT isomer deduplication, and Fisher-\(z\) desirability scoring (correlate_ion_taste_intensities(), plot_correlations(), prepare_taste_intensities_df()):

Mapped Kendall’s \(\tau\) to the Pearson-equivalent scale via Greiner’s relation \(r_{\text{eq}} = \sin(\frac{\pi}{2}\tau)\) (greiner_kendall = TRUE).
Deduplicated 2D InChIKeys within local retention-time windows (rt_window = 0.5 min) rather than globally across the chromatographic run, preserving resolved isomers such as Sweroside (id_ion = 3640).
Ranked feature-taste candidates by sample-size-adjusted Fisher-\(z\) desirability \(\text{sign}(r)\tanh(\frac{1}{3}\text{atanh}(|r|)\sqrt{\max(1, n - 3)}) S_{\text{TIMA}}\).
Completed the fraction x taste grid (complete_grid = TRUE) with baseline imputation (imputation_factor * min_v) and added configurable BH-FDR scope (fdr_scope = c("window", "taste", "global")).

Harmonized consistency filtering and multiplicative RMS panelist scaling (load_consistent_profiles(), plot_informed_tasting()): Filtered descriptors on harmonized taste_harmonized instead of raw taste_original (recovering METALLIC and CARTON) and added multiplicative RMS juror scaling plus session panel-size weighting (normalize_panelists = TRUE).
Two-pass sentinel harmonization and synonym aggregation (harmonize_terms(), prepare_profiles()): Protected matched dictionary spans with sentinel tokens (\x01<idx>\x02) to prevent shorter patterns from overwriting already-translated substrings, rescaled FIZZ > 10 export artifacts before deduplication, and aggregated synonymous ratings per (ProductName, CJ, newName) via max(value, na.rm = TRUE).
Napping MFA supplementary word block and Ward HCPC (plot_napping()): Projected the descriptor contingency table as a supplementary group (num.group.sup = n_coord_groups + 1L, type = "s") in FactoMineR::MFA() and switched FactoMineR::HCPC() from "centroid" to "ward".
Weighted simple network graph (plot_descriptors_network()): Collapsed parallel duplicate edges into edge weights (weight) before layout computation while preserving total vertex in-strength (size).
1D proton NMR chemometrics (cluster_nmr()): Excluded range_exclude_area prior to total-area normalization, merged detected peak positions closer than peak_width_ppm / 2, preserved sub-threshold areas as 0 for Hellinger + ward.D2 clustering (dist_method = "euclidean"), and aligned sorted dendrogram leaf colors to fraction labels via labels(dend).

title: sapid
text:
Bug Fixes & Hardening

Sensory dictionary & harmonization (harmonize_terms(), dictionary_specific): Switched mode = "word" to PCRE Unicode-aware boundary lookarounds ((*UCP)), escaped regex metacharacters, and filtered empty/NA patterns so accented French terms (ACIDITÉ, BOISÉ, FRUITÉ, SALÉ) and leading hyphens match accurately; repaired UTF-8 mojibake in dictionary_specific.
Package attach hook (.onAttach()): Passed lib.loc = libname with tryCatch() around utils::citation() so loading sapid from a custom library directory succeeds.
Spreadsheet & sensory loaders (read_xlsx_base(), load_session(), prepare_chasselas(), prepare_profiles()): Resolved worksheets via workbook.xml relationships, formatted Excel date serials from styles.xml, stripped <rPh> phonetic runs, handled self-closing empty rows and missing r= coordinates cleanly, excluded metadata ID columns (CJ, Date, Code, Session) from numeric pivots, fixed unreachable FIZZ >10 scaling in prepare_profiles(), and separated RAW: vs HARM: deduplication keys so distinct unmapped descriptors (newName = NA) are preserved.
Greiner correlation & plots (correlate_ion_taste_intensities(), plot_correlations(), plot_profiles()): Recorded "kendall_greiner" as the correlation method once Greiner’s \(\sin(\frac{\pi}{2}\tau)\) transform is applied so downstream plot_correlations() calls never transform correlation coefficients twice; sorted fraction factors numerically across plots.
Napping device isolation (plot_napping()): Captured FactoMineR and SensoMineR base-graphics output inside an isolated PDF device with on.exit() restoration, preventing stray Rplots*.pdf files and leaked graphics devices.
Psychometrics & concentration validation (fit_afc_psychometric(), plot_concentration(), sigmoid()): Coerced character concentration columns before rounding and sorting, excluded NA responses from panel sample sizes (n), aligned percentage axis labels, and validated positive integer counts in fit_afc_psychometric() plus smooth > 0 and n >= 2 in sigmoid().

text: This article covers 1D proton NMR spectral clustering, LC-MS/CAD chemical profiling, and rolling-window ion-taste correlation analysis.

title: 2 Chemical profiling & ion-taste correlations
text:
1D proton NMR clustering
cluster_nmr() processes Bruker 1D proton NMR spectra across fractions with four chemometric steps:

Pre-normalization solvent exclusion: excludes range_exclude_area (e.g., residual DMSO-\(d_6\) at 2.5–2.6 ppm) prior to AlpsNMR::nmr_normalize().
Peak position merging: merges detected peak positions closer than peak_width_ppm / 2 before integration.
Zero-preserving Hellinger + Ward.D2 clustering: sets sub-threshold areas (<= area_min) to 0, applies the square-root Hellinger transformation, and clusters with Euclidean distance (dist_method = "euclidean") and ward.D2 linkage.
Leaf-to-fraction alignment: matches sorted dendrogram leaf colors back to fraction labels via labels(dend).

cluster_nmr(
  nmr_dir = "./data/10043",
  output_figure = "./data/figures/figure_nmr.pdf",
  output_groups = "./data/groups.tsv",
  dist_method = "euclidean"
)

title: 2 Chemical profiling & ion-taste correlations
text:
Rolling-window ion-taste correlations
correlate_ion_taste_intensities() correlates LC-MS feature peak areas with sensory taste intensities across contiguous fraction windows (widths = 5:9):

Complete fraction x taste grid (complete_grid = TRUE): evaluated fractions where a taste was not reported receive the baseline imputed intensity (imputation_factor * min_v) rather than dropping out of sliding windows.
Normality-guided correlation: uses Pearson’s \(r\) when both vectors pass Shapiro-Wilk normality (\(p > 0.05\)) and Kendall’s \(\tau\) otherwise.
Greiner’s relation (greiner_kendall = TRUE): maps Kendall’s \(\tau\) onto the Pearson-equivalent scale via \(r_{\text{eq}} = \sin(\frac{\pi}{2}\tau)\).
Configurable FDR scope (fdr_scope): applies Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment per "window", per "taste", or "global".

Candidate ranking & isomer preservation (plot_correlations())
plot_correlations() combines correlation results with TIMA structural annotations:

Local RT-window deduplication (rt_window = 0.5 min): collapses co-eluting adducts and in-source fragments sharing a 2D InChIKey within each 0.5 min bin while preserving distinct chromatographic isomers (e.g., retaining Sweroside id_ion = 3640 in bitter fractions 34-39).

title: General comments about the use of SAPID
General comments about the use of SAPID
text:
Workflow overview

Vocabulary harmonization & panel scaling:

harmonize_terms() and harmonize_terms_df() standardize free-text French panelist terms using length-ordered two-pass sentinel token replacement (\x01<idx>\x02) so shorter patterns never overwrite already-translated substrings.
prepare_profiles() corrects FIZZ > 10 scale export artifacts prior to deduplication and aggregates synonymous ratings per panelist and sample via max(value, na.rm = TRUE).
load_consistent_profiles() retains descriptors used by at least min_jury distinct panelists and optionally applies multiplicative root-mean-square (RMS) juror scaling (normalize_panelists = TRUE).

Psychophysics & sensory evaluation:

plot_concentration() fits a guessing-corrected 3-AFC binomial log-logistic psychometric model (\(P(c) = \gamma + (1 - \gamma)\Lambda(\beta(\log_{10} c - \mu))\) with \(\gamma = 1/3\)) to estimate the 50% true detection threshold (\(\text{EC}_{50}\) at \(P = 2/3\)) and delta-method 95% confidence ribbons.
plot_chasselas_modulation() evaluates paired before/after wine modulation using Pratt’s (1959) zero-preserving Wilcoxon signed-rank test (test_method = "pratt").
plot_informed_tasting() compares classical raw-extract tasting against gravimetrically reconstituted fraction tasting using harmonized panelist-normalized intensities.
plot_napping() performs Procrustes MFA (SensoMineR::pmfa()), MFA with descriptor word contingencies as a supplementary block (FactoMineR::MFA()), and Ward’s hierarchical clustering (FactoMineR::HCPC(method = "ward")).
plot_descriptors_network() builds a simple weighted directed graph of sample fractions, original panelist terms, and harmonized descriptors.

1D proton NMR & LC-MS/CAD correlation:

cluster_nmr() excludes solvent regions prior to total-area normalization, merges detected peak positions within peak_width_ppm / 2, and clusters fractions using Hellinger distance (dist_method = "euclidean" on square-root areas) with ward.D2 linkage.
correlate_ion_taste_intensities() and plot_correlations() compute rolling-window correlations across contiguous fractions, map Kendall’s \(\tau\) onto the Pearson-equivalent scale via Greiner’s relation \(r_{\text{eq}} = \sin(\frac{\pi}{2}\tau)\), deduplicate co-eluting 2D InChIKeys within local retention-time windows (rt_window = 0.5 min) to preserve chromatographic isomers, and rank candidates via a sample-size-adjusted Fisher-\(z\) desirability score.

title: sapid
text:
A Strategy to Analyze Plant Extracts Taste in Depth (SAPID).
sapid integrates sensory panel data (free profiling, projective napping, Chasselas model-wine modulation, and 3-AFC recognition threshold testing) with untargeted LC-MS feature tables, Charged Aerosol Detection (CAD) semi-quantification, taxonomically informed metabolite annotations (TIMA), and 1D proton NMR spectral clustering. It accompanies the study of Swertia chirayita bitter extracts published in Current Research in Food Science (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.crfs.2025.101043).


Install sapid along with its CRAN, Bioconductor, and R-universe dependencies:
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("BiocManager", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
install.packages(
  "sapid",
  repos = c(
    "https://adafede.r-universe.dev",
    "https://taxonomicallyinformedannotation.r-universe.dev",
    BiocManager::repositories(),
    "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  )
)



The bundled datasets let you run descriptor harmonization and panel consistency filtering immediately after installation:
library(sapid)

title: sapid
text:
Replace terms in a character vector using a dictionary, ordering matches by decreasing pattern length with case-insensitive normalization and two-pass placeholder protection to prevent cascading overwrites.



harmonize_terms(dictionary, x, mode = "word", fallback = FALSE)







dictionary


Path to a dictionary TSV/CSV file or a data.frame containing original and translated (or translated_simple) columns.




x


Character vector to be harmonized.




mode


Replacement mode: “word” for word-boundary matching, “substring” for regex partial matching, or “fixed” for literal matching.




fallback


Logical; if TRUE, replace NA values with the uppercased input string.






Patterns are sorted in strictly decreasing order of character length so that multi-word expressions (e.g., “MINERAL AMER”) are matched before their constituent single-word tokens (e.g., “AMER”). Matched spans are first replaced by sentinel tokens (<idx>) and expanded in a second pass so that shorter patterns later in the dictionary cannot accidentally match substrings inside already-translated target terms.



Character vector with harmonized terms.




library("sapid")

data(dictionary_generic)
harmonize_terms(dictionary = dictionary_generic, x = "amer")

[1] "BITTER"

text:
Hierarchical record of sample preparation and fractionation of Swertia chirayita, documenting parent-child relationships and mass (in milligrams) at each step. Useful for tracking sample lineage and mass balance through extraction and purification.



fractions




A data frame with 94 rows and 3 columns:


parent


Parent fraction identifier (NA for root material)


label


Child fraction or processing step identifier


mass


Mass in milligrams at this stage





The hierarchy starts with raw plant material and initial solvents (EtOH, water) and traces through extraction, decanting, drying, and sub-fractionation steps leading to final analytic samples (V_01, V_02, etc.).



doi:10.1016/j.crfs.2025.101043; Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/14616396




library("sapid")

data(fractions)

title: sapid
text:
Compute rolling-window correlations between LC-MS feature peak areas and panel-consistent sensory taste ratings across contiguous chromatographic fractions, automatically selecting Pearson or Kendall correlation based on Shapiro-Wilk normality tests and applying Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment.



correlate_ion_taste_intensities(
  input_ions = "./data/fractions_mzmine/fractions.csv",
  input_tastes = NULL,
  output = "./data/correlations.tsv",
  min_jury = 2L,
  min_area_ion = 1L,
  imputation_factor = 0.5,
  widths = 5:9,
  complete_grid = TRUE,
  normalize_panelists = FALSE,
  greiner_kendall = FALSE,
  fdr_scope = c("window", "taste", "global")
)







input_ions


Path or data.frame of mzmine feature areas across fractions.




input_tastes


Optional path or data.frame of sensory profiles (defaults to built-in profiles).




output


Path to write the resulting TSV correlation table.




min_jury


Minimum number of distinct jurors required for a taste term (default 2L).




min_area_ion


Minimum feature peak area threshold (default 1L).




imputation_factor


Multiplicative factor applied to the minimum observed intensity when imputing missing values (default 0.5).




widths


Integer vector of rolling fraction window widths (default 5:9).




complete_grid


Logical; if TRUE (default), complete the fraction x taste grid across evaluated fractions using baseline imputation (imputation_factor * min_v).




normalize_panelists


Logical; if TRUE, apply RMS scale normalization per juror before summing (default FALSE).




greiner_kendall


Logical; if TRUE, map Kendall’s \(\tau\) to Pearson-equivalent scale via \(r = \sin(\frac{\pi}{2}\tau)\) and mark those rows with method = “kendall_greiner” so downstream functions do not apply the transformation twice (default FALSE).




fdr_scope


Scope of Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment: “window” (default), “taste”, or “global”.






Path to the written output TSV file.




library("sapid")

correlate_ion_taste_intensities()
